summary.name: Volt
summary.one_liner: Volt is an open-source agentic development workspace that combines an editor, Git, terminal, and AI coding agents in one app.
keywords: run multiple llm models in editor

reviewing what changed in each agent turn

managing Git and terminal alongside AI agents
summary.what_it_does: Volt unifies a code workspace, editor, Git tooling, and terminal in one interface, with AI coding agents built in. It runs external agents such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Grok, Antigravity, and Kimi Code using the user's existing sign-in, so the user keeps their own plan. The page says it can also connect to many model providers and local runtimes, including Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, OpenRouter, and Amazon Bedrock. It shows a change view that groups each file under the agent turn that modified it, with lines added and removed. The page describes it as highly inspired by Cursor and open source, and offers a curl install script.
notable: Runs existing agent subscriptions (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) instead of selling tokens
Per-turn change view showing files and line diffs for each agent turn and subagent
Broad model provider and local model support
caveats: Public beta, so features may be unstable
Using third-party agents requires your own existing sign-in or plan with those providers
